quizzes.stem: A review service sends thirty scanned pages, each 3000 pixels wide, in a single call, and the API refuses it with an invalid_request_error that cites a stricter limit for crowded requests. Which repair does the page document?

options.a: Send the pages from Amazon Bedrock, which accepts them without any per-image limit
options.b: Raise the output limit so that the reply has room to describe all thirty of them
options.c: Convert each page to GIF so that the stricter size limit stops counting it
options.d: Downscale each file to 2000 px or less per side, or cap the batch at twenty

explanation.d: The page says to resize each image "so that neither dimension exceeds 2000 px, or keep the request to 20 or fewer image and document blocks."
explanation.b: Ruled out because the stricter limit is "a stricter per-image dimension limit", which concerns the size of each file and not the reply.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Animations are unsupported, and only the first frame is used", which changes nothing about the dimension limit.
explanation.a: Ruled out because on Amazon Bedrock "only base64-encoded sources are currently available", and the limit still applies to every image.

quizzes.stem: A scanned A4 page is 1075 by 1520 pixels, both sides under the 1568 edge limit. On a standard-tier model, Claude points at (462, 654) for the signature line, yet the click lands above and to the left of the line on the original. What explains the miss?

options.a: The picture it viewed was 924 by 1307, so every returned value needs rescaling by that size
options.b: The reply was normalized to a 0 to 1000 grid and was then used as plain pixels
options.c: Claude pads every image on the top and left, which moved the origin downward
options.d: Pictures under the edge limit are returned untouched, so the model misjudged the line

explanation.a: The page works the example: 1075 by 1520 costs 2145 tokens, so on the standard tier it "is resized to 924 by 1307" and the point is in that picture.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Claude does not work well when you ask for normalized coordinates", and it returns pixel positions.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the padding sits "on the bottom and right", so the origin does not move.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "The token limit can resize an image whose sides are both under the edge limit."

quizzes.stem: A support agent keeps ten screenshots in a long chat and attaches all of them as base64 on every turn. Latency climbs with each turn. What does the page recommend?

options.a: Re-encode them as heavily compressed JPEG until the payload shrinks to a few hundred kilobytes
options.b: Move to a model with a larger window, which makes the repeated bytes cost nothing
options.c: Upload each one once and refer to it by id, so the payload stays small
options.d: Place the screenshots after the text, because that order shortens the transfer

explanation.c: The page says that an uploaded file keeps the payload small "regardless of how many images accumulate in the conversation history."
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Lossy compression can add artifacts that hurt text".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the problem is that "each request resends the full conversation history", whatever the window size.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the placement advice is only that Claude "works best when images come before text".

quizzes.stem: A team sends a 400-page annual report full of tables, and the call fails long before 600 pages. According to the documentation, what is the likely cause?

options.a: Tables are rasterized at a resolution that the API charges for separately
options.b: Heavy graphics and small type use up the context window first
options.c: PDFs above 100 pages are refused unless a beta header is present
options.d: Extracted text is capped at 1,000 tokens per document on every platform

explanation.b: The page says that dense PDFs with small-font pages or heavy graphics "can fill the context window before reaching the page limit".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Standard API pricing applies with no additional PDF fees."
explanation.c: Ruled out because the limit is "600, and 100 when the request's context window is under 1M tokens", and no header is involved.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the 1,000-token figure belongs to a mode that "uses roughly 1,000 tokens for a 3-page PDF" on Bedrock Converse and is not a cap on documents.

quizzes.stem: A multi-tenant application stores every customer's uploaded contract with the Files API and keeps one file id per customer in its database. Which design choice protects the customers from one another?

options.a: Encrypt each id with a customer key before it is stored
options.b: Give every file the shortest expiry that the API allows
options.c: Delete the files after each request and upload them anew
options.d: Give each client its own workspace in the organization

explanation.d: The page says that "a multi-tenant application creates a workspace for each tenant" because files are visible to the whole workspace.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A `file_id` is a capability: whoever can name it in a request in that workspace can read the file", whatever the stored id looks like.
explanation.c: Ruled out because a file uploaded anew is still "accessible to the whole workspace, not scoped to an end user, a conversation or a session", so re-uploading creates no boundary.
explanation.b: Ruled out because an expiry is something you set "at upload and not changed afterwards", and it does not separate tenants.

quizzes.stem: A user asks for one summary that covers an Excel workbook and a CSV file. How should the application prepare them?

options.a: Attach both as document blocks exactly as they are, since the API opens every format
options.b: Upload the delimited data as text/plain and convert the spreadsheet first
options.c: Convert each of them to a PDF, which is the only type a document block takes
options.d: Paste the spreadsheet bytes into a text block and rely on the model to decode them

explanation.b: The page says to upload `.txt`, `.csv` or `.md` "to the Files API with the MIME type `text/plain`", and that binary formats such as `.xlsx` and `.docx` "are not supported in document blocks".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Binary formats such as `.xlsx` and `.docx` are not supported in document blocks".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "A plain text file can go into a document block too", so a PDF is not the only type.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the page tells you to "convert them to text or PDF first" and offers no route that pastes raw bytes into a text block.

quizzes.stem: A mobile app uploads photos of receipts and the cost per request is higher than expected on a model in the high-resolution tier. Which statement from the module explains it?

options.a: Receipts can be billed as documents, which carry a flat surcharge per page
options.b: A single image can use up to roughly three times more visual tokens there
options.c: Every image can be charged a fixed amount whatever its size
options.d: The tier can charge for padding rows as separate tokens at a higher price

explanation.b: The first page says that "High-resolution images can use up to roughly three times more visual tokens than the same image on a standard-tier model".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Standard API pricing applies with no additional PDF fees."
explanation.c: Ruled out because "The price of an image is its token count times the model's input price", so size matters.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "The padding holds no content", and the cost is the token count of the image.

quizzes.stem: An agent returns a bounding box for a table on a scanned page, and the box sits slightly off when drawn on the original. The team divided the coordinates by the extent of the padded picture. What is the correct divisor?

options.a: The dimensions of the resized image, which is the one Claude saw
options.b: The next multiple of 28 above the resized width and height
options.c: The width and height of the original scan, taken before any resizing
options.d: The token limit of the tier, which is the same on both axes

explanation.a: The first page says: "Always normalize or rescale by the resized dimensions, not the padded dimensions."
explanation.c: Ruled out because the point Claude returned lies in the resized picture, and "a 1920×1080 screenshot resizes to 1456×819" shows that the original size differs from it.
explanation.b: Ruled out because that is the padded size, and "The padding holds no content".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the budget is a token count, and the page says only that "the visual token limit is what determines the final size", which is not a length in pixels.

quizzes.stem: A pipeline must stay safe if a new image source quietly produces larger pictures that Claude would shrink. Which feature of the API turns that silent change into an error?

options.a: A transformations setting that rejects any oversized input outright
options.b: The beta header that switches on high-resolution processing
options.c: Token counting, which refuses any image that would be resized
options.d: A smaller output limit, which makes resized images fail the call

explanation.a: The first page says that setting `"transformations": {"oversized_image": "error"}` makes the API reject an image that would be resized, "with a `400`, instead of resizing it."
explanation.b: Ruled out because "High-resolution support is automatic on the listed models and requires no beta header or client-side opt-in."
explanation.c: Ruled out because "a successful count doesn't mean the image is within the Messages API's request limits".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the documented behaviour is rejection "instead of resizing it", and no output limit is involved.

quizzes.stem: A contract workflow sends one PDF per request and wants the same document answered from many requests over a week, without re-sending its bytes. Which combination follows the module?

options.a: Host it at a public URL and pass the URL, since Bedrock prefers links
options.b: Embed it as base64 in every request and enable the stricter image limit
options.c: Upload it to the Files API, refer to it by id, and keep tenants in separate workspaces
options.d: Convert it to GIF frames so each page counts as a single small image

explanation.c: The pages combine the Files API, where "the payload stays small" and an id replaces the bytes, with "a workspace for each tenant".
explanation.b: Ruled out because base64 resends the bytes on every request, and "a stricter per-image dimension limit applies" is a limit to stay under and not a feature.
explanation.a: Ruled out because on Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud "only base64 sources are available", so a link does not work there.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Animations are unsupported, and only the first frame is used."
